sapience_notes.subject: Sapience's read-side and write-side project-scoping parameters are deliberately asymmetric
sapience_notes.value: sapience-retrieve.sh (read) sends project_cid, a server-honored strict pre-filter gated on the REPO_LINK_FOR flag (deployed off for this account, so unexercisable live, stub-verified only). sapience-remember.sh (write) sends a plain project key resolved from the same binding's cid via a GET /v1/people/projects lookup, and never project_cid -- a verified project_cid write is deliberately held shut by a separate governing ruling (sf1-engine ruling 7) regardless of the read-side flag's state, because two named leak surfaces for an unverified autonomous write stay open. The two sides do not converge even though they resolve the same binding file.

sapience_notes.subject: The installed vendor mcp.py's sapience_remember project argument is unrelated to per-repo tagging
sapience_notes.value: ~/.sapience/mcp.py's sapience_remember tool accepts a project argument, but it is company-store ROUTING (project_slug()/route_ko() matched against config.json's routes map, falling back to COMPANY_PROJECT/SAPIENCE_PROJECT) -- it picks which token/store a write posts to, not a per-repository [repo:<slug>] tag. It still cannot produce a tagged write, for the same connector-hardcoded-provenance reason the MCP write tools generally cannot. This had gone undocumented in per-repo-scoping.md prior to this phase despite the tool existing in the installed client all along.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh's OWED fallback set covered this phase's prose-only file at zero extra cost
sapience_notes.value: Running verify-touched.sh on a pure-documentation-plus-index-metadata change (per-repo-scoping.md prose, index-entries.json line_count) triggered both an explicit SELECT set (6 suites, directly mapped) and a 98-suite OWED fallback pass for the untestable prose path, all cost-class free -- 104 total suites passed with no manual suite selection needed and no full run-all.sh invocation.
